title: Teaching Elder Rodney King, et al. v. Presbytery of Western Carolinas
disposition_detail: Sole material issue: complaint that Presbytery's one-year wait before receiving a petition for organization was unjust, arbitrary, prejudicial, and beyond the BCO—not sustained. The General Assembly adopted the Judicial Commission's report (10 for, 1 abstaining); the vote on sustaining the complaint was 1 for, 12 against. The dissent recommending sustain and annulment was admitted but not adopted.
first_summary: A complaint alleged Presbytery's one-year delay before accepting a petition to organize a mission congregation was unjust, arbitrary, and beyond the BCO. The Judicial Commission did not sustain the complaint, citing BCO 5-1(1) discretion, the group's mission-only application, and the availability of Presbytery reconsideration. A dissent recommended sustain and annulment, but was not adopted.
summary: A complaint challenged Presbytery's one-year delay before accepting a petition to organize a mission congregation. The General Assembly adopted the Judicial Commission's report and did not sustain the complaint. It reasoned BCO 5-1(1) gives Presbytery discretion over the time for organization, the group had sought only mission status, and the dispute was best handled at Presbytery, where complainants could seek reconsideration. A dissent recommending sustain and annulment was admitted but not adopted.

sources.supports: Case caption, complaint, adopted Judicial Commission report, vote and reasons, dissent, and recorded negative votes.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: Source lines 1–5, 11, 41–43, 83. Caption: Teaching Elder Rodney King, et al. v. Presbytery of Western Carolinas; this is Complaint #4. The 9th General Assembly approved and accepted the Judicial Commission's statement and judgment as the Assembly's action and ordered it entered (lines 43, 83).
evidence_notes.dispute: Source lines 13–35, 99. The complaint targets the April 25, 1981 Presbytery action imposing a one-year wait before Presbytery could receive a petition for organization after receiving the Covenant Reformation Fellowship as a mission; complainants alleged the action was unjust, judgmental, arbitrary, prejudicial, and beyond the BCO.
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: Source lines 69, 73–83. Vote on sustaining the complaint: 1 for, 12 against. Adopted explanation: BCO 5-1(1) gives Presbytery discretionary authority over the time and date for organization; the group had applied only to be a mission; complainants could ask Presbytery to reconsider; and the matter was best handled at Presbytery. The report was adopted 10 for, 1 abstaining.
evidence_notes.qualifications: Source lines 93–127, 131–133. The dissent was admitted to record but not adopted; it recommends sustaining the complaint and annulling the action. Several commissioners requested that their negative votes be recorded. No adopted merits rationale appears beyond the majority explanation.
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: No incorporated judicial decision. Attachment A/Appendix A and Presbytery minutes are referenced (lines 21–23, 55, 61, 97) but are not included in the supplied source.
